cells.tense: The practice is lit now, and the one tending it is here with the pen.
cells.act: clear the ground of what came down
cells.ask: When a piece of this practice stops holding, clear what it leaves — put it away and leave the floor open instead of rebuilding, then see where the next step lands.
cells.core:
The work aims at something you can name, which is why the repetition doesn't feel like a treadmill. You're in fog where the next step is all that shows, and you take it anyway, at the bench or the desk or the mat, wherever the work happens. Nothing is forced. The hours alone with it don't close you off — they connect you to something, and the refining serves you instead of eating you.

This balance feeds what comes next, and what it's ready to feed is clearing. When something stops holding — an old way of doing it, a rule kept past its use — take it down instead of propping it back up. Put the piece away and leave the floor open. Watch where the next step lands from there. What falls needed to fall, and that isn't a loss; it's the practice doing what practice does.
cells.sheetLine: The work aims somewhere, and you're holding the aim.
cells.verb: keeping a small practice lit by hand
cells.place: in fog where you can see only the next step

cells.tense: Tomorrow has already arrived in the head, and the practice is braced against it.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Choose one grip in this practice — a streak, a number, a way it has to look — and put it down for three days. Tend the practice, not the grip.
cells.core:
In fog where only the next step should show, you're trying to see the whole road. Every session has a future you standing over it, correcting the grip, raising the bar, and the refining has stopped serving the practice. It serves the fear of stopping. Time alone with it has stopped being chosen and started feeling necessary, as though the work holds only while your hand is on it.

What you're gripping isn't the practice — it's the standard. Choose one grip, a streak or a number or how it has to look, and set it down for three days. Put down the grip, not the work. You'll reach for it; that's how you'll know it was there. Letting go of this isn't defeat and it isn't loss. The grip was not what kept the light on, and three days from now you'll know that by feel.

cells.tense: Practice once put something at risk, and you have stood at that door since.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Look at one patch of time this practice gets — an hour, a whole evening — and adjust it until the share is fair, then leave it alone without going back to check.
cells.core:
The practice hasn't held, and the door you're standing at is already behind you. Big resolutions, fresh starts, another run at it — none of it stuck, and something underneath assumes starting again asks more than it gives. In fog where the next step is all anybody gets, no step looks safe enough, so none gets taken. The habit of showing up is still there, in the shape of what you avoid.

What's out of proportion is the share: this has been all or nothing, and nothing has been winning. Take one patch of time the practice gets — an hour, an evening — and adjust it until the size is fair, attended to once, then left alone. No going back to check whether it was right. Right-sized and released, it stops being a debt and becomes a trade you can keep making.

cells.tense: You are already practicing, and the pen is down in a room where the writing happens.
cells.act: dream it from what you have already lived
cells.ask: Take ten minutes to picture this practice working out ahead, built only from pieces you've already lived. Let it form without checking it against a plan, and keep the picture.
cells.core:
The skill is real, and it arrived with nobody's name on it. There's no routine to point to and no discipline to defend — the thing shows up when it's needed, and you shrug about where it comes from. In fog where only the next step is visible, you're moving well and calling it luck. Cultivation has been running here with no author standing at it.

Sit with the picture for ten minutes. Imagine this working out ahead, using only pieces you've already lived — no new plan, no new person you'd have to become. Let it assemble itself, then keep it. That's the same line come back to its simpler form, and it puts a name on something you can see happening: this has been yours, and you have been walking it.
cells.sheetLine: The skill is real, and you've been calling it luck.

cells.place: in fog where you can see only the next step

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's practice has ever stopped; Too Little only supports that sustaining it has not held, and I say it that way. Too Much could be objected to as describing ordinary ambition rather than a fear of stopping — I keep it to what a night looks like and let them refuse it. The asks survive a wrong read: each is one small act with a clock at most a week, and none of them needs the reading to be true to be worth trying. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'The expertise is real, and it arrived without your name on it' — I've left it in Unacknowledged because the record's own face is misattributed authorship, not a compliment.
